cross_disciplinary_pairing.description: Akanna stands in for the extension officer who can only reach a village once a month. It pairs a small offline language model with hand written crisis playbooks for drought, pests, flooding, livestock disease, storage loss, and price crashes, so a farmer gets an answer the same day the problem shows up, not weeks later.

test_prompts.prompt: My maize leaves are curling and turning pale three weeks after the rains stopped early. The soil is cracking. What should I check first, and what can I do this week with only what I already have on the farm?

I found small holes and sawdust-like droppings in the whorls of my young maize plants, and a few seedlings look chewed and ragged. Is this fall armyworm, how do I confirm it, and what are my cheapest options before it spreads across the field?

model.name: Akanna-1.5B-Q4_K_M
model.adaptation_method: system prompt grounding with a local retrieval layer, no fine-tuning

tagline: An offline farm crisis advisor for the phone in your pocket and the laptop on your desk
